gaps.sentence: Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.

gaps.sentence: ___ you mind if I opened the window?
gaps.hint: a polite request with would you mind
gaps.explanation: 'Would you mind if' is followed by the past form for politeness: Would.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: You ___ smoke anywhere inside the building — it is strictly forbidden.
gaps.hint: strictly forbidden, which calls for mustn't

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: You ___ take an umbrella — the forecast says heavy rain all day.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' recommends a sensible action: should take.

gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.
